content: Zanamivir is prescribed for adults and children to treat certain types of influenza (commonly known as the flu) in individuals who have experienced flu symptoms for less than 2 days. It is also used to prevent certain types of flu in people who have been in close contact with someone infected with the flu or during a flu outbreak. Zanamivir belongs to a class of medications called neuraminidase inhibitors. It works by reducing the duration of flu symptoms, such as nasal congestion, sore throat, cough, muscle aches, fatigue, weakness, headache, fever, and chills. Zanamivir is available as a powder for oral inhalation. To treat influenza, the recommended dosage is two inhalations twice daily for 5 days. On the first day of treatment, your doctor may advise you to take the doses closer together. To prevent the spread of influenza within a household, two inhalations are taken once daily for 10 days. For community-wide flu prevention, two inhalations are taken once daily for 28 days. When using zanamivir for flu prevention, it should be inhaled at approximately the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use zanamivir exactly as directed, and do not use more or less of it or use it more frequently than prescribed. Zanamivir is provided with a plastic inhaler device called a Diskhaler, along with five Rotadisks (circular foil blister packs containing four doses of medication each). Do not puncture or open any medication blister pack until you are ready to inhale a dose using the Diskhaler. Carefully read the manufacturer’s instructions on how to prepare and inhale a dose of zanamivir using the Diskhaler. If you have any questions about its use, ask your pharmacist or doctor. If a child is using the inhaler, an adult who has been instructed by a healthcare provider on its proper use should supervise the child. Continue using zanamivir even if you start feeling better, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. If your symptoms worsen, new symptoms develop, or your flu symptoms do not improve, contact your doctor immediately. Zanamivir may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before using zanamivir, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to zanamivir, any other medications, foods, or lactose (milk proteins). Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had asthma, other breathing problems, bronchitis, emphysema, heart disease, kidney disease, liver disease, or other lung conditions. If you use an inhaled medication for asthma, emphysema, or other breathing problems, take your regular medication before using zanamivir if they are scheduled at the same time. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking zanamivir, contact your doctor. Be aware that zanamivir may cause serious or life-threatening breathing problems, particularly in patients with asthma or emphysema. If you experience difficulty breathing or wheezing after taking zanamivir, stop using it and seek medical attention immediately. If you have been prescribed a rescue medication for breathing difficulties, use it immediately and then call for medical help. Do not take any more zanamivir without consulting your doctor. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while using zanamivir. If you forget to take a dose, inhale it as soon as you remember. If it is within 2 hours of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not inhale a double dose to make up for a missed one. Zanamivir may cause side effects. Mild side effects include headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, cough, nasal irritation, and infections of the ear, nose, sinuses, throat, or bronchi. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects include difficulty breathing, wheezing, shortness of breath, hives, rash, itching, difficulty swallowing, swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs, and hoarseness. If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store zanamivir in its original container, out of reach of children, at room temperature, and away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Maintain proper hygiene, wash your hands frequently, and avoid sharing cups or utensils to prevent spreading the flu virus. Ask your doctor if you should receive an annual flu vaccination, as zanamivir does not replace the need for a yearly flu vaccine. The Diskhaler should only be used for zanamivir and not for other inhaled medications. Your prescription is likely not refillable.
